findings.text: The hypervisor offers a version three interrupt controller CPU interface emulator that claims trapped system accesses only for virtual machines configured for that controller version. It reports handled with a positive outcome and declined with zero, leaving declined exits to other handling.

The hypervisor offers a version two interrupt controller CPU interface proxy for data abort exits. It emulates accesses inside the virtual CPU interface window against the hypervisor mapping and advances the guest past the instruction on success.

A fast system register path claims an exit when any special case applies, giving errata workarounds precedence over interrupt controller emulation and virtual counter reads. Unclaimed exits proceed to normal handling.

Trap handling dispatches through a table indexed by exception class. Each entry accepts the virtual CPU plus exit code and reports whether it consumed the exit, with missing entries treated as declined.

Guest exit fixup records fault syndrome except for interrupts, corrects the return address for hypercalls when an asynchronous error is pending, and invokes trap handling only for trap exits without pending errors. Consumed exits resume the guest while others return to the host.

Low exception memory handling first tries to populate fault information. Data aborts then try version two controller emulation for valid translation faults without external or walk faults, converting rejected emulation into an asynchronous error exit.
32 bit coprocessor exits attempt version three controller emulation when enabled and otherwise decline to normal handling.

Version three emulation enforces direction per register group. Acknowledge and related status reject writes, completion and related controls reject reads, while enable and priority controls accept both directions through dedicated helpers. Successful emulation advances the guest past the trapping instruction.

Deactivation handling depends on overflow request and interrupt mode. With overflow requested the hypervisor attempts in place clearing of the matching list entry and resumes only on success. Clearing is skipped when completion and deactivation are split and for identifiers in the software range.

Nested forwarding applies only in nested contexts. One group follows one trap all control, the other group follows another, deactivation follows its own control with fallthrough to common controls, and common controls follow a common trap control. Enable registers also honor fine grained read and write controls.

Virtual counter reads serve physical and virtual counts computed from the hardware physical count minus a per timer offset. They apply only for 64 bit guests outside hypervisor context and honor nested trap controls. Successful reads deliver the value to the destination register and advance the guest.
The observed register write tail accepts translation and memory attribute controls and writes them through to shadow state, advancing the guest on success and declining unknown encodings.
The same write tail accepts fault reporting controls and writes them through similarly, advancing on success and declining unknown encodings.

On affected parts, translation control writes are intercepted to clear hardware managed bits before write through, preserving architectural reservation when the feature is unadvertised, then the guest advances.
For 32 bit guests, version three emulation validates the instruction condition first. A failing condition advances the guest without emulation and reports handled.

Version two proxying builds the fault address from the intermediate address plus the high fault offset, requires containment in the CPU interface window, rejects non word or misaligned accesses, and leaves the deactivation range to full exit handling.
Guest byte order for version two proxying follows processor state for 32 bit guests and system control for 64 bit guests, with symmetric swapping applied on reads and writes.

List lookup scans only the used prefix for an entry with matching virtual identity and active state, reporting a spurious value on miss. Clearing removes active state and for hardware backed entries performs physical deactivation using the encoded physical identity before writing the entry back.
The virtual machine control value used during emulation is sourced from the hypervisor control interface register.

Processor state synchronization preserves saved state across a single step erratum by rewriting saved status when stepping coincides with a pointer authentication trap, then always captures current saved status into the register file.

Unexpected hypervisor exceptions search a dedicated table for an instruction address matching the current return address and redirect there on hit. On miss the return address is preserved in hypervisor context and execution vectors to a restore and panic path.

Debug and overlay state uses indirection for debug control when the context is a guest with host owned debug. Common save and restore handle that control plus the overlay register when overlays are present, ordered early because the overlay can affect host access.
Reliability state is treated as present only when the platform capability is final and the virtual machine enables it.

Exception return state save and restore cover program counter and status plus virtual error syndromes, selecting host or nested storage by nesting and reliability presence. Restoration maps hypervisor modes to host modes and forces an illegal state status when privileged 64 bit return is requested, then programs return registers and syndrome.
The hypervisor page pool record holds a spinlock, a set of free lists indexed by page order, a physical address range, and a maximum order value.
The pool spinlock serializes concurrent updates to pool metadata and to page descriptors of pooled pages until a proper atomic interface exists at this exception level.
The host translation record aggregates architecture state, a stage two table, table operation callbacks, and a spinlock field.
Protected mode identity distinguishes host, hypervisor, and guest principals as three enumerated values in that order.
Firmware interface function numbers span inclusive 0x60 through 0xFF.
The no order sentinel is the all ones eight bit value.
Host stage two loading installs the host translation when protected mode is initialized and otherwise clears the translation base register.
Ownership self test is an empty operation accepting a base pointer.
Version two proxying treats non word or misaligned accesses as illegal, advancing the guest while reporting an error that the abort path promotes to an asynchronous error exit.

Restoration targeting privileged 64 bit mode never returns there. It programs an illegal state status that faults immediately after exception return, with 32 bit hypervisor returns faulting through execution state rules.
Secure monitor wrappers for the two specification versions bracket the call with exit tracing before and entry tracing after, using a null context and a monitor reason.
Clock tracing is inert with an empty update and a zero read. Event scaffolding defines a per name identifier record in a dedicated section with cleared enable state, plus an empty multi read marker.
Observed headers are idempotent through include guards. Early allocation and generic memory headers expose no additional behavior in these fragments beyond their guards.
